title: Purpose, result, and infinitive
subtitle: Distinguish an aim from the action that follows a governing verb.
overview: An infinitive may complete a governing verb or express purpose; ἵνα and ὥστε offer other ways to state intended outcome and result.
Map the main action first. Then ask whether the next verbal form names what someone does, intends to do, or what comes about.

sections.title: Three relationships
rows: so that he may proclaim: purpose clause
with the result that they were amazed

items.en: He went out to a deserted place to pray.
These things have been written so that you may believe.
